# ROM GUARD

> A dataset covering one question about Xiaomi ROM flashing: can you undo it?
> No ROM files are hosted and no flashing instructions are published.
> Non-commercial, no ads, no affiliate links.

## Policy

- Two conditions make a device permanently unrecoverable: an Anti-Rollback (ARB) eFuse violation,
  and dropping to EDL (9008) without an authorized Mi Account.
- ROM files are never mirrored: no redistribution right, GPL source obligations, and mirroring
  makes the host the publisher if a build is compromised.
- A field with a value must carry a source URL and a verification date. Unverified fields stay null.
  Enforced at build time, not by convention.
- Hashes are computed from files downloaded here. Hashes transcribed from upstream pages are rejected.

## Regions

Firmware ships per market and what you lose by leaving your region's build differs by country:
carrier VoLTE profiles and band tables everywhere, FeliCa on Japanese units, additional account
binding on mainland-China units. Radio-equipment certification and warranty law also differ —
follow the laws that apply where you are.

## Data

- [Devices](https://romguard.pages.dev/data/devices.json): unlock policy, EDL auth, ARB, FeliCa, LineageOS
- [Rules](https://romguard.pages.dev/data/rules.json): reversible vs irreversible, ROM types, writable layers
- [Hashes](https://romguard.pages.dev/data/roms.json): SHA-256 records of distributed ROM files

## Pages

- [Check](https://romguard.pages.dev/) — run before flashing
- [What cannot be undone](https://romguard.pages.dev/risk/) — ARB, EDL, relocking
- [Hash records](https://romguard.pages.dev/verify/) — how to check a download, and what it does not catch
- [Devices](https://romguard.pages.dev/devices/) — including unverified fields
- [About](https://romguard.pages.dev/about/) — policy and disclaimer

## Note

No warranty. Flashing can render a device permanently unusable.
